perf.summary: Find uses recursive path compression with AggressiveInlining (which cannot apply to recursion); convert to an iterative two-pass path-compression to avoid call overhead and stack growth, and drop the misleading inline hint.
perf.currentCost: Recursive Find on the DSU is called per edge and per BFS neighbor (Find(parent, to[e])). Each Find is a recursion with a write-back; deep chains cost call frames. The AggressiveInlining hint is inert on the recursive call.
perf.proposedChange: Make Find iterative: walk to root with a local loop (int r = i; while (parent[r] != r) r = parent[r];), then a second loop to compress (while (parent[i] != r) { int nxt = parent[i]; parent[i] = r; i = nxt; }). Remove AggressiveInlining or keep only on the now-small iterative leaf.
perf.rationale: Iterative path compression has the same amortized inverse-Ackermann complexity but no per-level call frame, shorter dependency chains, and is Burst-friendly (no recursion to a non-inlinable callee). Hottest DSU primitive called O(edges + BFS-visits) times.
perf.risk: Must preserve full path compression semantics (all nodes on path point to root) to keep amortized bounds; the two-pass form does exactly that. Observable parent[] end-state equals the recursive version's. Safe.

perf.summary: Union does parent[rootI] = rootJ with no union-by-rank/size; combined with path compression the DSU loses the near-constant amortized guarantee and can degrade Find chains, directly slowing AddEdge's per-edge Find and the contraction loop.
perf.currentCost: Unbalanced union can create long parent chains before compression kicks in, increasing Find cost across the many Find calls in the BFS (Find(parent, to[e]) per edge traversed) and in the contraction loop.
perf.proposedChange: Add a rank or size array (caller-provided int* to honor the no-hidden-state rule) and attach the smaller tree under the larger in Union. Init alongside parent in Init. This keeps Find chains shallow.
perf.rationale: Union-by-rank/size + path compression gives O(alpha) amortized; without rank, worst-case Find chains grow, raising the cost of the per-edge Find calls that dominate AddEdge. Asymptotic/amortized improvement on the hot path.
perf.risk: Changes the signature/Init contract (adds a rank buffer) — an API change the caller must adopt; flag as ergonomics-affecting. Behavior of SCC results is identical (DSU connectivity unchanged); only internal tree shape and speed differ. Medium risk due to signature change.

perf.summary: In the contraction loop, Union(parent, node, rootU) recomputes Find(parent, rootU) for every visited node even though rootU is fixed; hoist Find(parent,rootU) once and union each node's root into it directly.
perf.currentCost: The loop calls Union qt times; each Union does Find(node) and Find(rootU). rootU's root is invariant across the loop but is re-derived each iteration (and rootU is already a root at loop start, though compression during the loop can move it).
perf.proposedChange: Since rootU is a DSU root at the start and the loop only attaches others under it (parent[rootI]=rootJ direction), compute the target root once: keep merging into rootU and set parent[Find(parent,node)] = rootU directly, recomputing only node's root. If union-by-rank is added this needs care, but for the current attach-into-rootU semantics the rootU Find is redundant.
perf.rationale: Removes qt redundant Find(rootU) calls in the contraction loop, each of which (with current unbalanced DSU) may walk a chain. Cuts work proportional to visited-set size per cycle contraction.
perf.risk: Current Union always points rootI under rootJ; calling Union(node, rootU) attaches node's root under rootU's root. Inlining as parent[Find(node)] = rootU is equivalent ONLY while rootU remains a root — it does, because nothing is ever attached above it in this loop. Verify before applying; without rank this holds. Low-medium risk.
